name: S800
summary: Honda was best known for motorcycles when it built this tiny roadster, and it showed. The 791 cc four made its power at 8,000 rpm, and early cars still drove the rear wheels through a chain.

name: Civic
summary: A compact front-wheel-drive hatchback that arrived just before the 1973 oil crisis. From 1975, the optional CVCC engine could meet tightening emissions rules without a catalytic converter or unleaded fuel.

name: CR-X
tagline: Short, light and cut off at the tail
summary: A short, light hatchback with a low nose and an abruptly chopped rear. From September 1989 the second generation offered the B16A outside North America, making it the second Honda with a DOHC VTEC engine, just after the Integra XSi.

name: NSX
summary: The first production car with an all-aluminium semi-monocoque, nearly 200 kg lighter than a steel equivalent. Ayrton Senna advised the engineers during final tuning at Suzuka and pushed for a stiffer chassis. The 1992 NSX-R was the first Honda to wear the Type R name.

name: Civic Type R EK9
summary: The first Civic to wear the Type R badge, sold only in Japan. Honda started from the three-door SiR, left out the sound deadening, seam-welded the shell for rigidity and added a helical limited-slip differential. The 1.6-litre B16B made its power at 8,200 rpm.

name: S2000
summary: Launched in April 1999 for Honda’s 50th anniversary, with a name that continues the S500, S600 and S800 line. The F20C revved to a 9,000 rpm fuel cut and made about 124 hp per litre, the highest of any mass-production naturally aspirated car until 2010.
